doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

title: Recent and upcoming projects: self-released record and Jerry Bergonzi
summary: Bailey describes her YouTube and vinyl release, new work with Jerry Bergonzi, Taurus Power, and an Anat Cohen tour.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Do you have coming next projects in mind?

Yeah. Well I just put this record out and I did it in a different way. It’s on YouTube so I can tell you’ve been checking it out. It’s free on YouTube and there’s a whole series with it. It’s still dropping over the summer. It’ll still be there. It’s also on vinyl so I thought let’s do this, which is doing well, it’s actually selling really well. And digital downloads through me. So I said hey I want to take back control of this. There’s one tune, “Block Up” is streaming so you can get that on iTunes and stuff. So this is sort of an experiment. It’s been interesting. So that’s sort of ongoing. I just — I have something new coming out, I just started working with Jerry Bergonzi which is incredible. I mean wow what a moment to work with him. So we have something coming out with him on a record he has coming out on Savant I think this fall. Harvie S., Phil Grenadier and Luther Gray. And then we recorded something very recently, I don’t know when that will come out, probably later next year. And then a project — we just played at Small’s — it’s called “Taurus Power” and it’s with my friend Marian McSweeney, longtime buddy and collaborator, a great bass player, great composer. So it’s the two of us with Jerry Bergonzi as our special guest. Mike Fahn on valve trombone and Austin McMahon on drums. So we’re mixing that right now so we’re looking at maybe releasing that maybe next spring either on vinyl or whatever. But things are coming up, are Jerry Bergonzi’s release in the fall. So I’m very excited — I mean to me he’s the top of the mountain in terms of musicianship and God, just virtuosity, but also generosity and kindness as an artist, composer, educator. He’s just — it’s been an amazing experience to meet him and become part of his musical family.
It’s wonderful when you find — how many saxophone players are there out there — and you find someone who in particular plays your music in ways that you hadn’t even imagined.

Yeah, yes. Well he’s — I mean he’s an amazing composer. He’s so prolific and he’s so open just I mean as a person. But he brings that to the music. He’s a great mentor and influence in my life right now.
Well you’ve had a number of those which is a terrific thing over the years.
Yeah, and also we have something with Anat Cohen — we’ll be touring in early 2024 — God 2024 — yeah we’ll have a West Coast tour. And I hope that we’ll have some new
